# Help wanted: add primary sources for non-EU/US regimes to the reading list

Labels: help wanted, chapter-10, reading-list

## The gap

The reading list's "Regulation and standards" section (`bok/10-reading-list.md`) is strong on the EU
and the US but thin on the rest of the world. Chapter 08 already cites the South Korea AI Basic Act
[34] and Singapore's IMDA framework [39], yet neither has an entry in the reading list, and China's
AI rules appear nowhere in the book (see the companion regulatory-map issue). A reader who works
across Asia-Pacific has no primary-source starting point here.

## What to add

Add primary-source entries to the "Regulation and standards" section of `bok/10-reading-list.md`,
matching the existing bullet format (bold title — one-line description — backticked URL — verified
tag):

- South Korea — the AI Basic Act (official or authoritative English source).
- Singapore — the IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI.
- China — the official texts named in the regulatory-map issue (generative-AI interim measures,
  deep-synthesis and algorithmic-recommendation provisions, AI-content labelling measures).

Reuse an already-verified `sources/SOURCES.md` row where chapter 08 already cites the instrument,
rather than re-verifying (`STYLEGUIDE.md` §6).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each entry follows the reading-list bullet format and carries a verification tag.
- Primary sources link to the official text where one is reachable; otherwise use a reputable
  secondary source and tag it `secondary`.
- Entries added for instruments already cited in a chapter reuse the existing `sources/SOURCES.md`
  row and its tag.
